Narration transcript
  1. 0:00 Think like a photographer. Every Auto Optimize choice is a photographer's decision, made in code.
  2. 0:06 Shutter vs. ISO. With a fixed aperture, exposure trades shutter for ISO: fast freezes motion but adds noise, slow blurs it.
  3. 0:15 Meter for the subject. Averaging the frame turns a backlit face into a silhouette. Meter for the face, and let the window blow out.
  4. 0:24 Protect the highlights. Clipped highlights hold no data. Crushed shadows can be lifted, with some noise. So guard the highlights first.
  5. 0:33 Tone curves make the look. Most pro looks are tone curves. An S-curve adds contrast; lifted blacks and soft highlights feel like film.
  6. 0:42 White balance has two axes. White balance has two axes: blue to amber, and green to magenta. A gray card reads neutral when it's right.
  7. 0:51 Protect skin tones. Skin of every complexion sits near one line. Push a global grade and faces drift magenta, so protect that range.
  8. 1:00 Read the light. Front light is flat, side light shows texture, back light makes a rim. Small sources light hard, large ones soft.
  9. 1:09 Composition basics. Rule of thirds, a level horizon, leading lines and headroom. Each one makes a good guide overlay.
  10. 1:17 Know the pipeline. Apple's ISP processes every frame before your code sees it. Shoot RAW alongside to see what it did.
  11. 1:26 Build a hard-scene test set. Test every change on the scenes that break cameras, then shoot manually for a week. That habit is what Auto Optimize automates.
